companies.name: NVIDIA Corporation
companies.summaryEnHtml:
NVIDIA is a US semiconductor company organised into two segments: Compute & Networking — GPU compute and networking, sold mainly into data centres — and Graphics. Compute & Networking is by far the larger business: in FY2026 (ended January 2026) it produced US$193,479mn of revenue, 89.6% of the group total, against US$22,459mn (10.4%) for Graphics. Group revenue in FY2026 was US$215,938mn (+65.5% YoY) and operating profit US$130,387mn. By customer headquarters location, the United States accounted for 69.3% of revenue, Taiwan 19.6% and China (including Hong Kong) 9.1%. NVIDIA employed 42,000 people at the FY2026 year-end and spent US$18,497mn on R&D in the year.

Growth has accelerated since: in Q3 FY27 (quarter ended 25 Oct 2026) revenue reached US$115.8bn (+103% YoY), of which Data Center was US$107.6bn (+110% YoY), 93% of sales, and Q4 FY27 revenue was guided to US$130.0bn ±3% as Vera Rubin NVL72 systems began shipping (company results, 17 Nov 2026). Founder Jensen Huang, who resigned as CEO on 11 Nov 2026, was reinstated as President and CEO by the board on 23 Nov 2026.

エヌビディアは、米国の半導体メーカーです。事業は2つのセグメントで構成されています。コンピュート＆ネットワーキングは、主にデータセンター向けにGPUコンピューティングとネットワーキングを提供する事業です。もう1つはグラフィックス事業です。2026年1月期の売上高は、コンピュート＆ネットワーキングが1,935億ドルと全体の89.6%を占め、グラフィックスは225億ドル（10.4%）でした。グループ全体の売上高は2,159億ドルで、前年から65.5%増えました。営業利益は1,304億ドルでした。顧客の本社所在地別では、米国が69.3%、台湾が19.6%、中国（香港を含みます）が9.1%でした。2026年1月期末の従業員数は42,000人で、同年度の研究開発費は185億ドルでした。

その後もデータセンター向けの成長は加速しています。2027年1月期の第3四半期（2026年10月25日に終了）には、売上高が1,158億ドルとなり、前年同期から103%増えました。うちデータセンター向けは1,076億ドル（同110%増）で、全体の93%を占めました。第4四半期の売上高見通しは1,300億ドル±3%であり、Vera Rubin NVL72の出荷が始まっています（2026年11月17日の会社発表に基づきます）。創業者のジェンスン・フアン氏は2026年11月11日にCEOを辞任しましたが、同年11月23日に取締役会の決定で社長兼CEOに復帰しました。

companies.name: Fujikura Ltd.
companies.summaryEnHtml:
Fujikura is a Japanese manufacturer of cables and optical products, organised into five segments. The largest is Information & Communication — optical fibre, fusion splicers and data-centre cabling — followed by Automotive Components, Electronics, Energy and a small Real Estate business. AI data-centre demand has made Information & Communication the group's profit engine: in H1 FY3/27 (Apr–Sep 2026) the segment generated ¥217.7bn of operating profit, up 195.0% YoY, accounting for almost all of the group's profit pool (company results, 10 Nov 2026).

In FY3/26 (ended 31 Mar 2026) revenue was ¥1,182,358mn (+20.7% YoY) and operating profit ¥188,707mn (+39.2%). Segment revenue was Information & Communication ¥652,977mn (55.2% of revenue; segment profit ¥152,729mn, a 23.4% margin), Automotive Components ¥179,370mn (15.2%), Electronics ¥172,305mn (14.6%), Energy ¥156,983mn (13.3%) and Real Estate ¥11,032mn (0.9%). By customer location, the United States was the largest market at ¥522,200mn (44.2%), ahead of Japan at ¥241,425mn (20.4%). FY3/27 company guidance, revised at the November 2026 Q2 print, stands at revenue ¥1,768,000mn and operating profit ¥429,000mn.

フジクラは、電線と光製品を手がける日本のメーカーです。事業は5つのセグメントで構成されています。最大の情報通信事業は、光ファイバ、融着接続機、データセンター向けの配線を扱います。ほかに自動車部品、電子部品、エネルギー、不動産の各事業があります。AIデータセンター向けの需要が拡大し、情報通信事業がグループの利益の中心になりました。2027年3月期の上半期（2026年4月から9月）には、このセグメントの営業利益が2,177億円となり、前年同期から195.0%増えました。グループの利益のほぼ全体をこのセグメントが占めています（2026年11月10日の会社発表に基づきます）。

2026年3月期の売上高は1兆1,824億円で、前年から20.7%増えました。営業利益は1,887億円で、同39.2%増でした。セグメント別の売上高は、情報通信が6,530億円（全体の55.2%、セグメント利益は1,527億円、利益率は23.4%）、自動車部品が1,794億円（15.2%）、電子部品が1,723億円（14.6%）、エネルギーが1,570億円（13.3%）、不動産が110億円（0.9%）でした。顧客の所在地別では、米国が5,222億円（44.2%）で最大であり、日本が2,414億円（20.4%）でした。2027年3月期の会社計画は2026年11月の第2四半期決算で修正され、売上高1兆7,680億円、営業利益4,290億円となっています。

companies.name: Advantech Co., Ltd.
companies.summaryEnHtml:
Founded in Taipei in 1983 by KC Liu and two fellow Hewlett-Packard engineers, Advantech built its position in industrial PCs (IPCs) — ruggedised computers, embedded boards and systems designed for factory, medical, retail, transport and energy environments, sold on long lifecycles (typically 5–7+ years of supply commitment) rather than consumer-style refresh cycles. The portfolio spans embedded computing (boards, modules, edge systems), industrial automation (controllers, I/O, HMI), intelligent systems (medical and retail terminals, in-vehicle and railway systems) and service/solutions. The WISE-IoT software platform and the sector-driven 'AIoT co-creation' model — building solutions with ecosystem partners rather than selling boxes alone — are the company's stated route from hardware to platform economics, under the vision of 'Enabling an Intelligent Planet'.

Production is centred on Taiwan (including the Linkou AIoT campus) and Kunshan, China, supplemented by regional assembly and configuration centres; the new North America headquarters in Tustin, California, integrating local assembly, technical service and customer collaboration, began production in 2026 — a direct response to North America's order surge and to customers' localisation requirements. Advantech employs more than 9,000 people globally (company material; 9,478 per data vendors, Nov 2026).

companies.name: Tsugami Corporation
companies.summaryEnHtml:
Tsugami manufactures and sells precision machine tools, organised as a single product business (machine tools) reported through five geographic, entity-location segments. Its core is the CNC precision automatic lathe: in particular the sliding-headstock (Swiss-type) lathe, in which bar stock is supported by a guide bushing at the cutting point and fed through the spindle, allowing long, slender, small-diameter parts to be turned to micron-level tolerances without deflection. Tsugami began production and sales of sliding-headstock automatic lathes in 1957 and launched its Mercury CNC composite automatic lathe line in 1978 (company history, Tsugami corporate materials, accessed November 2026). Typical workpieces are small precision components for smartphones and other electronics, automotive parts, medical devices, watches and connectors — parts typically below roughly 38mm in diameter, produced in high volumes.

The product range, as disclosed in the tanshin sales-results note, has four lines. (1) Automatic lathes — ¥108,621mn in FY3/26, 84.1% of revenue — covering Swiss-type sliding-headstock models, CNC lathes and turning centres. (2) Grinding machines — ¥5,505mn (4.3%) — including cylindrical grinders. (3) Machining centres, thread-rolling machines and special-purpose machines — ¥8,886mn (6.9%). (4) Other — ¥6,127mn (4.7%) — parts and services. Product-line profit is not disclosed. Automatic lathes have held an 84–85% revenue share in every year of the sheet period (FY3/22: ¥79,504mn of ¥93,174mn, 85.3%), so the group is, in substance, a single-product company with small adjacent lines (Company results via PL/segment sheet (tanshin, JPX archive)).

companies.name: DMG Mori Co., Ltd.
companies.summaryEnHtml:
DMG Mori is a Japanese-German machine-tool group headquartered in Nagoya, Japan, and listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange (6141). It manufactures and sells CNC machine tools and provides the services around them — repair and restoration, spare parts, engineering, automation systems and software — through two reportable segments, Machine Tool and Industrial Services (segment definitions per the Q3 2026 tanshin, 30 October 2026; see Section 5).

The product range spans the core cutting-machine categories: machining centres (including 5-axis and horizontal models such as the INH series, extended in 2026 with the INH 63 FD turning-capable variant offered with either FANUC or Siemens controls), turning centres and multitasking (mill-turn) machines, additive manufacturing machines, and ultrasonic/laser machines, together with automation (pallet and robot systems), measuring technology and digital products. Group companies extend the range into adjacent precision equipment: Magnescale (linear scales), Saki Corporation (inspection systems for electronics mounting), Taiyo Koki (grinding machines) and DMG Mori Precision Boring (horizontal boring machining centres, which launched the PBN 200|1250 in 2026). The company's current product strategy, branded MX (Machining Transformation), pushes process integration — combining operations on one machine — plus automation and digitalisation (including its CELOS control interface and, from 2026, 'manufacturing physical AI' work selected under METI/NEDO's GENIAC programme, with an investment in the Japanese AI developer Noetra; Q3 2026 tanshin, 30 October 2026).

companies.name: Fanuc Corporation
companies.summaryEnHtml:
Fanuc is a single-segment company by its own statement in the tanshin: there is one reportable segment, and the business block of the PL/segment sheet therefore carries disclosed product-line sales only, with no product-line profit (profit by product line is not disclosed). The four product lines share one technology core — CNC controls and servo systems — one manufacturing footprint in Japan, and one global service network. All products are manufactured at four Japanese locations: the Oshino-mura headquarters campus at the foot of Mt Fuji (Yamanashi), Mibu (Tochigi), Tsukuba (Ibaraki) and Hayato (Kagoshima) (company disclosures as summarised in third-party company profiles, Nov 2026). Production is famously automated — robots building robots — and concentrated in Japan, which concentrates both quality control and yen exposure in one place.

In FY3/26 the sales mix was: Robot ¥378,610mn (44.1%), FA ¥208,478mn (24.3%), Service ¥141,143mn (16.5%) and Robomachine ¥129,600mn (15.1%) (Company results via PL/segment sheet (tanshin, JPX archive)). The mix has shifted over the cycle: Robot peaked at ¥380,944mn in FY3/24 even as group sales fell, while FA is the most cyclical line — ¥250,113mn in FY3/23, down 27.9% to ¥180,384mn in FY3/24, recovering to ¥208,478mn in FY3/26.

ファナックは、決算短信で会社自身が述べるとおり単一セグメントです。報告セグメントは1つだけで、PL/セグメントシートの事業ブロックには製品別の売上高だけが載ります。製品別の利益は開示されません。4つの製品群は、CNCとサーボシステムという1つの技術の核、日本国内の生産拠点、世界のサービス網を共有しています。生産はすべて日本国内の4か所です。富士山麓の忍野村にある本社地区（山梨県）、壬生（栃木県）、筑波（茨城県）、隼人（鹿児島県）です（2026年11月の第三者の企業プロフィールに基づく会社の開示）。生産の自動化は徹底し、ロボットがロボットを作る形で知られます。品質管理と円への露出が、同じく日本国内に集中しています。

2026年3月期の売上構成は、ロボット3,786億円（44.1%）、FA 2,085億円（24.3%）、サービス1,411億円（16.5%）、ロボマシン1,296億円（15.1%）でした（会社の決算短信に基づくPL/セグメントシート）。構成はサイクルの中で移ってきました。ロボットは2024年3月期に3,809億円で山を作り、グループの売上高が減る中でも伸びました。FAは最も景気に敏感な製品群です。2023年3月期の2,501億円から2024年3月期に27.9%減って1,804億円となり、2026年3月期に2,085億円まで戻りました。

companies.name: Amada Co., Ltd.
companies.summaryEnHtml:
Amada Co., Ltd., headquartered in Isehara, Kanagawa, is a comprehensive manufacturer of metalworking machinery — it develops, manufactures, sells, leases and services the machines, tooling, software and automation that turn sheet metal and metal stock into finished parts. Its customers are job shops and OEMs across automotive, electronics, construction machinery, aerospace, medical, energy and general fabrication. The group's own description of its two legacy businesses (FY3/26 tanshin) frames the portfolio: metalworking machinery (sheet-metal products and precision welding) and metal-cutting machinery (cutting, grinding and press products) — now reorganised into the five BUs described in section 2.

The core franchise is sheet metal. Flagship lines include fibre-laser cutting machines (the ENSIS series, using Amada's own fibre-laser oscillator with beam-control technology that processes thin and thick material from a single resonator; the REGIUS series at the high end), NC turret punch presses (EM Z series), press brakes and bending robots (EGB series and automated bending cells), shearing machines and combination punch-laser machines. Around the machines sits the automation layer — loaders, storage towers and sorting systems — and the software layer: VPSS 3i (Virtual Prototyping Simulation System), which simulates the full production process from 3D data before metal is cut, and SheetWorks 3D CAD. Joining Technologies covers fibre-laser and resistance welding, including precision (micro) welding for electronic components, batteries and medical devices. Cutting Fabricator & Grinding covers band saws and cutting machines (the group's founding product), carbide blades and profile grinders. Advanced Forming covers mechanical and servo presses, from Amada Press System's small and mid-size machines to H&F's large presses for automotive lines. Electronics Process is Via Mechanics' PCB drilling machines (mechanical and laser), aimed at package-substrate production for AI servers.

companies.name: Sodick Co., Ltd.
companies.summaryEnHtml: Sodick is a precision-machinery group headquartered at 3-12-1 Nakamachidai, Tsuzuki-ku, Yokohama, with capital of ¥24,618mn and 21 affiliated companies (company outline, FY12/25). Its founding business — NC electrical discharge machines — remains the core, but the group also makes high-speed machining centres and metal 3D printers (machine tools), injection-moulding machines (industrial machinery), noodle-making and packaged-rice plants (food machinery), and components and materials — linear motors, ceramics, NC units, EDM wire — that are both sold externally (in 'Other') and consumed in-house, giving the group an unusually high in-house production ratio for its key technologies.

companies.name: Yaskawa Electric Corporation
companies.summaryEnHtml: Yaskawa Electric is headquartered in Kitakyushu, Fukuoka Prefecture, and listed in Tokyo and Fukuoka. Since its founding in 1915 the group has defined its domain as 'electric motors and their applications', and today organises itself around three core technologies — motion control, power conversion and robotics — delivered through three reportable segments plus Other. The segment definitions below are the company's own (Q2 FY2/27 tanshin, segment note): Motion Control develops, manufactures, sells and services AC servo motors, control devices and inverters; Robotics develops, manufactures, sells and services industrial robots and related products; System Engineering develops, manufactures, sells and services industrial automation drives and social (infrastructure) systems. Segment profit is on an operating-profit basis. In FY2/26 the mix was Motion Control 43.5% of revenue, Robotics 45.6%, System Engineering 7.1% and Other 3.7% (external revenue basis, PL/segment sheet).

companies.name: Harmonic Drive Systems Inc.

companies.name: Kanadevia Corporation
companies.summaryEnHtml: Kanadevia is an Osaka-based plant-engineering and machinery group, founded in 1881 as Osaka Iron Works and renamed from Hitachi Zosen Corporation to Kanadevia Corporation on 1 October 2024 — the shipbuilding business that gave the old name its meaning was separated in 2002, and the last marine-engine link was deconsolidated in March 2026. The group reports three core segments plus Other: Environment (¥505,230mn of FY3/26 external sales, 78.3%), Machinery & Infrastructure (¥68,468mn, 10.6%), Carbon Neutral Solutions (¥69,238mn, 10.7%) and Other (¥2,284mn). Consolidated headcount was 12,666 at March 2026 (securities report compilation), of whom about 8,989 were in Environment. The organising idea across the group is the plant life cycle: engineer and build the facility (EPC), then operate, maintain and retrofit it for decades (O&M) — a model the company is extending into DBO (design-build-operate) contracts and, at Inova, into concessions and asset ownership.

companies.name: Lasertec Corporation
companies.summaryEnHtml: Lasertec, headquartered in Kohoku-ku, Yokohama, designs, manufactures and sells inspection and measurement systems, overwhelmingly for semiconductor photomask and wafer-related applications, and reports as a single segment. Its disclosed revenue categories are semiconductor-related equipment, services, and other products (principally flat-panel-display inspection and laser microscopes). Overseas sales are the large majority of revenue (third-party estimates put them at about 92% in FY6/25 — an estimate, not a company-disclosed ratio in the sources used here). The group's model is asset-light at the factory and heavy at the workbench: precision parts production is substantially outsourced, with final assembly, adjustment and inspection in Yokohama — including at the Lasertec Innovation Park (InnoPa, in operation since July 2023; Fab-4A/4B in production per Shared Research) — which is one structural reason gross margins near 60% are possible, and why work in process, not fixed assets, dominates the balance sheet.

companies.name: THK Co., Ltd.
companies.summaryEnHtml: THK is a machine-components manufacturer headquartered in Shibaura, Minato-ku, Tokyo. After the June 2026 transfer, its business is the industrial machinery business: the design, manufacture and sale of linear-motion and mechatronic components — above all the LM Guide — to machine-tool builders, semiconductor and flat-panel production-equipment makers, industrial-robot and general factory-automation builders, and medical, aerospace, railway and other precision-machinery users worldwide. The continuing company's demand is therefore a derived function of global manufacturing capex, with semiconductor equipment the marginal driver in 2026.

companies.name: Misumi Group Inc.
companies.summaryEnHtml: Misumi is headquartered in Tokyo (Chiyoda-ku) and organises itself into three reportable segments — FA, Die & Mold Components and VONA — unchanged across all ten years of this report. The segment definitions below are the company's own (tanshin segment notes): the FA business manufactures and sells FA components (factory-automation parts); the Die & Mold Components business manufactures and sells die components and mould parts; VONA is the distribution business, selling other manufacturers' products — production-equipment parts, manufacturing consumables and MRO (maintenance, repair and operations) indirect materials — alongside Misumi-brand products. Segment sales are external customer sales (intersegment sales are nil in every period); segment profit is on the operating-profit basis. In FY3/26 the mix was FA 36.4%, Die & Mold Components 20.0% and VONA 43.6% of sales, with segment profit of ¥20,283mn / ¥8,694mn / ¥18,635mn — VONA is the largest segment by sales and FA the largest by profit margin. The company's own description of its model, repeated across the tanshin qualitative sections, is that it combines a manufacturer business and a distribution business, using IT, logistics and manufacturing bases and a global network to serve customers' 'global, reliable, short lead time' needs and to remove inefficiency from manufacturing. The company states it sells more than 40 million products worldwide through its e-commerce platform (company website, accessed November 2026).

companies.name: Disco Corporation
companies.summaryEnHtml: Disco is headquartered in Ota-ku, Tokyo, and organises its entire business around three precision-processing technologies — Kiru (cutting/dicing), Kezuru (grinding) and Migaku (polishing) — applied to semiconductor wafers and advanced electronic materials. It states in every tanshin that it is a single segment and omits segment information; the product/service note is likewise omitted as identical to the segment (sheet register S3). No product-line sales split is disclosed in the tanshin, and none is presented as disclosure in this report; the only product split available is the shipments breakdown in briefing/press materials, used in section 3b and labelled as such. companies.name: Daifuku Co., Ltd.
companies.summaryEnHtml: Daifuku designs, manufactures, installs and services material-handling systems — the automated transport, storage and sorting infrastructure inside factories, distribution centres, semiconductor fabs, automotive plants and airports. The disclosed business fields (from the tanshin's qualitative text and the revenue disaggregation by industry) are: intralogistics systems for general manufacturing and distribution; cleanroom systems for semiconductor production lines; automotive production-line systems; airport systems; and electronic equipment through Contec (industrial computers and related products, whose sales are also the 'electronic equipment' line of the product/service note). The group's own demand framing (FY12/25 tanshin) is labour shortage and rising labour costs driving automation investment in Japan and the US, advanced-semiconductor investment including back-end automation on generative-AI demand, continued semiconductor localisation investment in China, high automotive investment centred on the US (with tariff-related timing delays), and airport automation investment on rising passenger numbers. Crucially for reading the accounts, the reportable segments are the core group entities, not these fields (register S4): the parent company (which itself spans intralogistics, cleanroom, automotive and airport work in Japan and exports), Contec, DNA, CFI and DSA, plus 'Other' — the remaining domestic and overseas subsidiaries, spanning material-handling subsidiaries in China, Taiwan, Korea, Thailand and India, car-wash equipment (Daifuku Plusmore) and sales/service subsidiaries across the Americas, Asia, Europe and Oceania. Segment profit is each entity's contribution on an owners'-net-income basis (register S5) — a definition with no analogue among the FA peers in this programme, and the reason segment margins in this report are never compared directly with operating margins.

In FY6/26 the mix was Products 46.0% of external sales and LABO 54.0%; a decade earlier (FY6/17) it was Products 63.1% and LABO 36.9% — the store business is the growth engine, the products business the margin engine. Head office is in Obu, Aichi Prefecture; the Products sales organisation runs eight sales offices (Sapporo, Sendai, Tokyo, Yokohama, Nagoya, Osaka, Hiroshima, Fukuoka, per the Q1 FY6/27 segment note's revenue decomposition) and 22 training centres nationwide (Q1 FY6/27 tanshin).

companies.name: West Holdings Corporation
companies.summaryEnHtml: West Holdings is a solar-centred developer-operator: it develops, designs, builds, owns, operates and maintains renewable-energy plants, and since FY8/25 develops and sells grid-scale battery storage. The group reports five segments from FY8/25 — renewable energy, grid storage, energy saving, electric power and maintenance — plus a small 'Other' (environmental-value/J-credit trading, placed in Other from FY8/26). Segment profit is operating profit before corporate adjustments. The FY8/25 revenue decomposition in the segment note shows the business model concretely: renewable energy = industrial solar EPC ¥12,644mn + non-FIT plant development ¥17,402mn + mega-solar (WEST FIT) ¥1,491mn + other revenue ¥1,130mn; electric power = green-power wholesale ¥1,547mn + sales from owned plants ¥4,613mn; maintenance = comprehensive management and O&M contracts ¥1,551mn (external basis). Flow revenue (EPC, development sales, storage sales) dominates; stock revenue (own-generation sales, ESCO, maintenance) is the smaller, steadier base the strategy aims to grow.

companies.summaryEnHtml: Hitachi's organising idea is 'Social Innovation' through the combination of IT, OT (operational technology) and products, increasingly delivered as Lumada — the company's digital solutions layer, now being re-based on the stricter HMAX definition (solutions meeting defined criteria for AI/data-driven recurring value). The former Green Energy & Mobility was split into Energy and Mobility, and Automotive Systems (Astemo) ceased to be a reportable segment. Sector profit is Adjusted EBITA; the definition was revised from FY3/26 (see Basis of preparation).

companies.name: Tokyo Electron Limited
companies.summaryEnHtml:
Tokyo Electron (founded 1963) develops, manufactures, sells and services semiconductor production equipment. Since FY3/2024 it reports a single segment — semiconductor production equipment — having previously reported SPE, FPD (flat panel display equipment) and Other (Chapter 5). The group's manufacturing and sales/service subsidiaries in Japan and overseas execute production, installation and field service.

The finest product split the company discloses shows what the single segment contains in a strong quarter. In Q2 FY3/2027 (July-September 2026), new equipment was about ¥734.4bn, roughly 79% of the quarter's ¥935.0bn of sales, with field solutions (parts, used equipment, modification and service) making up the balance. Within new equipment, non-memory applications (logic and foundry) were 56% of sales, DRAM 34% and non-volatile memory 10%. Geographically, the same quarter's presentation-basis sales were ¥339.9bn to China (36.4% of sales, up from 30.4% in Q1), ¥190.7bn to South Korea (20.4%) and ¥180.4bn to Taiwan (19.3%); management guides the full-year China share to the low-30% range, below the Q2 print.

companies.name: Nabtesco Corporation
companies.summaryEnHtml:
Nabtesco was formed in 2003 from the merger of Teijin Seiki and Nabco. It reports three segments plus an 'Other' category, organised as internal companies: the Component Solutions segment (precision reduction gears — the RV reducer line for industrial-robot joints and machine tools — and, until the 2026 transfer, hydraulics), Transport Solutions (railway vehicle equipment, aircraft flight-control components, marine control systems, and automotive components), Accessibility Solutions (automatic doors, platform screen doors, welfare equipment) and Other (packaging machinery, 3D modelling equipment and similar). Headquarters are in Hirakawa-cho, Chiyoda-ku, Tokyo. Representative Director, President & CEO is Kazumasa Kimura (in the role since 2023; Katsuhiro Teramoto is Chairman).

Capacity, not demand, is the disclosed constraint in the reducer franchise. The company puts precision-reducer capacity at 1.15 million units a year across the Tsu and Changzhou plants and the ramping Hamamatsu plant; in Q3 FY12/2026 utilisation was 85% at Tsu and 95% at Changzhou, with Hamamatsu output expanding gradually and its further expansion timing to be judged against demand because Tsu still has headroom. Reducer orders in Q3 were flat quarter on quarter but up 18% year on year, at what management called a past-peak level; it attributes the strength not to broad automotive capex, which it calls not strong, but to competition among Chinese automakers and to higher reducer unit prices. North American automotive robot demand, almost none last year on the company's account, is gradually starting to move in 2026 and is expected to contribute from FY12/2027.

companies.name: NSK Ltd.
companies.summaryEnHtml: NSK (founded 1916; headquartered in Shinagawa, Tokyo) is one of the world's largest manufacturers of bearings, with three reportable segments since September 2025: Industrial Machinery (industrial bearings, ball screws, linear guides, megatorque motors and condition-monitoring solutions), Automotive (bearings and automotive components including electric-brake ball screws) and Steering (electric power steering and steering columns through NSK Steering & Control), plus a small Other category. President & CEO is Akitoshi Ichii (Representative Executive Officer, in the role since April 2021); Keita Suzuki is CFO. NSK is a company with a nominating committee. In May 2026 NSK and NTN announced a basic agreement on a business integration (Chapter 8).

companies.name: NTN Corporation
companies.summaryEnHtml: NTN (founded 1918; headquartered in Nishi-ku, Osaka) manufactures bearings, constant-velocity joints and axles, and precision equipment. Its reportable segments are entity-location regions — Japan, Americas, Europe, Asia & other — while its product disclosure (from the FY3/2025 tanshin) splits sales into Bearings & others (¥348,890mn in FY3/2026) and CVJ / Axle (¥477,453mn). The earlier market-basis split (aftermarket / industrial machinery / automotive) was disclosed through FY3/2024 and is kept on its own basis in this report. President, Executive Officer & CEO is Eiichi Ukai (in the role since April 2021); Masaaki Yamamoto is CFO. NTN is a company with a nominating committee. On 12 May 2026 NTN and NSK announced a business integration via a joint holding company (joint share transfer) — Chapter 8.

companies.name: JTEKT Corporation
companies.summaryEnHtml: JTEKT (headquartered in Kariya, Aichi) was formed in 2006 from Koyo Seiko (bearings, steering) and Toyoda Machine Works (machine tools, driveline). It is a core Toyota-group supplier. President & CEO is Yoshihito Kondo (since June 2024; a Toyota production-engineering veteran, re-elected at the June 2026 AGM); Kazuyuki Kamiya is CFO. Segment profit is business profit — revenue less cost of sales and SG&A, after HQ cost allocation (register S3) — and the bridge from segment profit to IFRS operating profit is other operating income/expenses, which is where structural reform lives. Reportable segments were reorganised in FY3/2022 from the old two (Machine Parts & Components / Machine Tools) to the current three; the history block keeps the old basis for FY3/2017–21 and the two are never mapped into each other.

companies.name: Sumitomo Electric Industries, Ltd.
companies.summaryEnHtml: Sumitomo Electric Industries (founded 1897; headquartered in Kitahama, Osaka) is the Sumitomo group's electric-wire and materials house. President is Osamu Inoue. It reports five segments (segment profit = operating profit; register S3). The mix is unusually barbelled: a very large, low-margin automotive harness business (Sumitomo Wiring Systems) and a small, now very high-margin optical business, with power cable, electronic materials and carbide tools between them. A 4-for-1 stock split took effect on 1 July 2026.

President & CEO is Noboru Saito (since April 2022); CFO is Tetsuji Yamanishi. It reports four segments plus Other (segment profit as defined by the company — sales less cost of sales, SG&A and other operating items, excluding head-office costs; register S3).
